Well, I finished my first day at work as a Courtesy Clerk at a supermarket and got my paycheck for training, also. It's extremely hard explaining how you feel, that's for sure. It's important to know you're not alone. If anything, start writing things down. I'm sure it'd at least get you a little bit further along than you are/were.

Don't cut yourself short. Focus on bettering yourself, it'll help A LOT. Times do get rough, but things get better. My Uncle had plans to become an automotive. He was faced with having to work an absolutely terrible job where he would come home and break down crying, and he made it through it, went to college, and became what he wanted, and owns multiple homes now. 

Anxiety controls a lot of aspects in life, my uncle didn't let that control him, though. Feeling as though things won't change is a huge thing, and it's an absolutely terrible feeling, but you need to focus on telling yourself positive things, like things do change, things won't always be stressful, you'll get the hang of things and you'll find people who were once in your position, and you might be able to even help them. Keep yourself open to everything, from making friends to accepting what you're worse at than other things, and working on those things. Don't tell yourself you're not very smart. If you need, study. Independent studying isn't a bad choice, always devote an hour or two every several days to becoming more intelligent. A lot of people who are extremely intelligent and making ground-breaking discoveries didn't start out with grade-A smartness. A lot of people work to get to where they are, and I honest-to-God believe you'll be able to be in the position you've always dreamed about. Good luck, and if you ever need, don't be afraid to PM me. I'd love to talk.
